detailed_description:
The target video is a living sumi ink painting in <Subject 2>: every stroke keeps its wet brushed texture as it moves, ink flows and drips like real liquid ink on paper, and the hairline moon and cloud outlines stay thin, clean and steady.
[Shot 1] The shot begins from <Picture 1>. In slow motion the black cat rises through the air on a rising diagonal toward the moon, front paws reaching out and hind legs stretching long behind her as they leave the ground, her fur rippling in the rush of air. Her tail unrolls behind her into a huge swirling ribbon of wet black ink that sweeps around in a great arc from the lower left, spreading and flinging drops steadily across the paper through the whole shot. The moon brightens softly as she rises toward it. Every frame keeps her rough dry-brush ink texture, ragged wispy fur edges and white slash highlights; she is never a smooth, flat cartoon shape, and her motion is weighty and real, like a slow-motion wildlife shot. The camera tilts up at slow speed in one continuous, smooth move, lagging slightly behind her, the brush-stroke ground sinking out of the bottom of the frame and the full hairline moon settling into the right half. The camera is still tilting and the ink ribbon is still unfurling as the shot ends on <Picture 2>, the cat at the height of her leap. No cut or transition occurs.
